title: Binary search
description: The function binary_search looks for the number target in the ascending sorted list items and returns its index. If the number is not in the list, it returns -1.
bug_description: The loop condition while low < high stops the search when low and high are equal, so the last remaining candidate is never checked. The function returns -1 even though the number is in the list whenever the search narrows down to one remaining element: searching for 9 in [1, 3, 5, 7, 9] returns -1 instead of 4, and searching for 42 in [42] returns -1 instead of 0.
hints_json: Does the function find every number in the list, no matter where it is?
What does the function return when the list has only one element, and it is exactly the number being searched for?
Look at the while loop condition: what happens when low and high become equal?
fallback_feedback: The bug is in the loop condition while low < high. When low and high become equal, one candidate is still left, but the loop stops before checking it, so the function returns -1 even though the number is in the list. The loop must also run when low and high are equal.
